General Background and Product Offerings
Digi International Inc. ("Digi ® ," "we," "our," or "us") was incorporated in 1985 as a Minnesota corporation. We reorganized as a Delaware corporation in 1989 in conjunction with our initial public offering. Our common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market tier of the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (the "Nasdaq") under the symbol DGII. Our World Headquarters is located at 9350 Excelsior Blvd., Suite 700, Hopkins, Minnesota 55343. The telephone number at our World Headquarters is (952) 912-3444.
We are a leading global provider of business and mission-critical Internet of Things ("IoT") connectivity products, services and solutions. We help our customers deploy, monitor and manage critical communications infrastructures that deliver important information in demanding environments with high levels of security and reliability. We have two reportable segments under applicable accounting standards: (i) IoT Products & Services; and (ii) IoT Solutions.
Our IoT Products & Services segment offers products and services that help original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs") as well as enterprise and government customers create and deploy secure IoT connectivity solutions. These include embedded and wireless modules, console servers, enterprise and industrial routers as well as other infrastructure management equipment to meet our customers' IoT communication requirements. In addition, this segment provides our customers with device management platform services, as well as other professional services to enable customers to capture and manage data from devices connected to networks. In January 2026, we enhanced the offerings of this segment through our acquisition of Particle Industries, Inc., a provider of IoT connectivity and device management solutions for customer products that incorporate embedded modules.
Our IoT Solutions segment consists of our SmartSense by Digi® business and our Managed Network–as–a-Service (“MNaaS”) business acquired via our November 2021 acquisition of Ventus Wireless, LLC and affiliated entities ("Ventus"). SmartSense by Digi offers wireless temperature and other condition-based monitoring services. SmartSense by Digi also includes solutions offered under the Jolt® brand, including employee task management, workforce management and labeling solutions that we acquired in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 through our acquisition of Jolt Software, Inc. On September 30, 2026, we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Disruptive Technologies, a Norway-based provider of advanced sensing technology that is expected to further enhance the capabilities of SmartSense by Digi. Disruptive Technologies adds small form factor, low power sensors with long battery life to the SmartSense product portfolio, which we believe will make deploying sensing at scale easier and more efficient for our customers. Disruptive Technologies also expands the verticals served by SmartSense to include building and facility monitoring and provides the business with a European base of customers. SmartSense by Digi, including the Jolt offerings, focuses on the following vertical markets: food service, healthcare (primarily pharmacies and hospitals) and supply chain. Ventus® is a leader in the provision of MNaaS solutions that simplify the complexity of enterprise wide area network (“WAN”) connectivity for customers. The Ventus portfolio includes cellular wireless and fixed line WAN solutions for an array of connectivity applications in banking, healthcare, retail, gaming, hospitality and other sectors.
For more in-depth descriptions of our products and services, please refer to the heading "Principal Products and Services" at the end of Part I, Item 1 of this Form 10-K.
Our corporate website address is www.digi.com. In the "Company–Investor Relations" section of our website, we make our annual report on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, our annual proxy statement and any amendments to these reports available free of charge as soon as reasonably practicable after they are filed with or furnished to the United States Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"). Information on our website is not incorporated by reference into this report or any other report we file with or furnish to the SEC.
Industry and Marketplace Conditions
We believe the IoT industry is in the midst of a multi-year expansion as many industries are undergoing a digital transformation within their business that drives demand for IoT capabilities across a broad spectrum of services. Among others, IoT use cases include providing and maintaining secure connectivity and monitoring of operating assets in a wide range of businesses, condition-based monitoring of perishable goods, enabling remote work by employees and automating workflows and operations.
Our IoT Products & Services segment represented the majority of our sales in fiscal 2026. This segment sells both wired and wireless products that either are embedded into the products of OEMs or serve as stand-alone products. These offerings allow

Given the current uncertainty in macroeconomic conditions, including, but not limited to, potential recessionary conditions, the implementation of tariffs by governments around the world, changing global geopolitical conditions, evolving regulatory approaches to artificial intelligence, technology and digital infrastructure, supply chain disruptions globally and the uncertain status of large project-based customer deployment opportunities, our results during fiscal 2027 may be inconsistent quarter to quarter or with historical results.
Strategy
We remain focused on taking steps that we believe will deliver consistent, long-term growth with higher levels of profitability. This includes continuously reviewing and managing the product, service and solution offerings we provide to align with customer interests and to meet market demand. In addition, acquisitions historically have helped significantly advance our offerings and drive growth and profitability, in both business segments. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, we completed the acquisition of Jolt Software, Inc., and in January 2026 we completed the acquisition of Particle Industries, Inc., each of which enhanced our offerings and recurring revenue opportunities. On September 30, 2026, we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Disruptive Technologies. While it is possible we will complete smaller transactions, we primarily are focusing our efforts for future potential acquisitions on opportunities of scale with the potential to enhance subscription based recurring revenue.
IoT Products & Services Segment
Our IoT Products & Services segment is managed so our product management, research and development and sales personnel are aligned along specific product lines. We believe this management structure brings greater market focus and potential growth to our product lines. We also continue to drive efforts to pair our hardware offerings with our remote manager device management platforms as well as other support services such as Digi 360 and Digi LifeCycle Assurance. These bundled offerings are sold on a subscription basis and allow customers to monitor and manage the performance of hardware they purchase from us remotely. In January 2026, we enhanced these capabilities through our acquisition of Particle Industries, Inc. ("Particle"), a provider of edge-to-cloud application infrastructure for intelligent devices that incorporate embedded modules. Particle generated approximately $20 million of Annualized Recurring Revenue (“ARR”) at the time of acquisition and further advanced our strategy of expanding recurring revenue within this segment. As of September 30, 2026, the ARR of this segment was $64 million.

Summary of Risk Factors
Our business is subject to many risks and uncertainties, which you should consider before investing in our common stock. These risks are described more fully in Item 1A, "Risk Factors," and include the following:
Operational and Strategic Risks
• We depend on contract manufacturers and a broad set of suppliers, some of whom provide limited-source components. Supply chain disruptions, including component shortages tied to demand from artificial intelligence and data center build outs, could harm our customer relationships and profitability.
• Long and variable sales cycles make our operating results hard to predict.
• Parts of our business depend on a small number of customers or on particular industries.
• We may not successfully integrate acquired businesses, including Jolt and Particle, or realize the expected benefits of those acquisitions.
• Defects or failures in our products, software or services, especially in mission-critical uses, could expose us to claims and harm our reputation.
• Our growing reliance on software, cloud-based and subscription offerings creates execution, competitive and service-availability risks.
• Changes in tariffs and trade policy could raise our costs and make our products less competitive.
• Our IoT Solutions businesses operate in emerging markets and face added risks.
• We depend on strategic relationships with third parties and on keeping key personnel.
Technology and Cybersecurity Risks
• AI tools may let threat actors find and exploit vulnerabilities in our products and infrastructure faster than we can respond.
• Cybersecurity incidents affecting our products, cloud platforms or internal systems could increase our costs and damage our reputation.
• Our use of artificial intelligence could lead to regulatory or legal action or reputational harm.
International, Regulatory and Industry Risks International, Regulatory and Industry Risks
• Our reliance on foreign suppliers and our international operations expose us to geopolitical, trade, sanctions, currency and compliance risks, including under the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and the UK Bribery Act 2010.
• We depend on wireless networks and carrier certifications, and changes in spectrum or licensing rules could hurt our products.
• Failing to comply with environmental, data privacy, cybersecurity and other regulations could reduce our revenue.
• Natural disasters, wars and other events beyond our control could disrupt our supply chain and customers.
Competitive and Market Risks
• We face intense competition from companies that may have greater resources, and rapid technological change could make our products obsolete.
• Economic downturns, uneven timing of customer purchases and declining margins on mature hardware products could hurt our results.
• We may not be able to protect our intellectual property, and our use of open source software, third-party software and AI-assisted coding could limit our rights or expose us to claims.
Financial and Common Stock Risks
• Failing to comply with the covenants in our credit facility could limit our access to capital or cause a default.
• Unexpected tax changes or additional tax liabilities could affect our results.
• The price of our common stock may be volatile, and unsolicited takeover proposals or activism could distract management. A sustained drop in our market value could lead to a goodwill impairment.

Operational Risks
We depend on manufacturing relationships and a broad set of suppliers, some of whom provide us with limited-source components and parts, and disruptions in these relationships may cause damage to our customer relationships or otherwise negatively impact our business.
We procure all parts and certain services involved in the production of our products and subcontract most of our product manufacturing to outside firms that specialize in such services. Although most of the components of our products are available from multiple vendors, we have several single-source supplier relationships, either because alternative sources are not available or because the relationship is advantageous to us. Supply chains globally continue to experience disruptions and constraints due to a range of factors, including geopolitical tensions, changing trade policies and tariffs, export controls, transportation disruptions and shortages of certain semiconductors, memory components and other components associated with investments in artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure. These disruptions have affected and may continue to affect our ability to procure inventory, components and services in a timely and cost-effective manner. While inventory levels have generally returned to historical ranges, disruptions in global supply chains or component availability could adversely affect our operations, customer relationships and profitability. Supply-chain disruptions in recent years, including those associated with the COVID-19 pandemic and its aftermath, affected our ability to procure certain inventory and services and, at times, required us to maintain inventory levels above historical norms in order to meet customer demand. The impacts of these circumstances driven by supply chain stress were material in some instances and it is possible additional material impacts could occur in the future. There can be no assurance that our suppliers will be able to meet our future requirements for products and components in a timely fashion. In addition, the availability of many of the components we need is dependent in part on our ability to provide our suppliers with accurate forecasts of our future requirements. Delays or lost revenue could be caused by other factors beyond our control, including late deliveries by vendors of components, or force majeure events. As an example of force majeure, a fire many years ago disrupted the operations at one of our contract manufacturers in Thailand. If we are required to identify alternative suppliers for any of our required components, qualification and pre-production periods could be lengthy and may cause an increase in component costs and delays in providing products to customers. Any extended interruption in the supply of any of the key components or the availability of manufacturing services that currently are obtained from limited sources could disrupt our operations and have a material adverse effect on our customer relationships and profitability.
The long and variable sales cycle for certain of our products and services makes it more difficult for us to predict our operating results and manage our business.
The sale of our products and services may require a significant technical evaluation and commitment of capital and other resources by potential customers and end users, as well as delays frequently associated with end users’ internal procedures to deploy new technologies and to test and accept new technologies.
